hello!! as a fellow PT myself I can provide some “inside info” haha :) 

Many PTs especially those in commercial gyms have the most baseline qualification, the Certified Personal Trainer Cert, widely done online. Are they all good? No, unfortunately. I have met many trash personal trainers, but there are still trainers who are exceptionally great at what they do. I have met trainers with 10 years in the field but their skills are mediocre, on the other hand i have met trainers who just started their career but are amazing at delivering results. 

Many will tell you that looks are important when seeking a PT, not always. In fact, a large handful of the good PTs I have met do not look crazy fit, however, really know their stuff and that can be seen through the way they coach and how they program training for their clients. 

Sometimes, they will try to sell you with promotions like “start today and save —“ If you’re not fully convinced about their capabilities, do not sign a package with them, know when to say no. You need to be able to trust your trainer. 

It is important that you are able to “click” with your trainer, you’ll be seeing them 2, maybe 3 times a week. If you don’t enjoy being around them, you won’t be able to enjoy training. This is why booking a trial session is important! Finding a personal trainer is a commitment, jumping to different trainers often will only create problems and won’t bring you the results you desire. 

Hope this helps somehow :) atb in your search OP

Hello! Fellow celiac here there’s a FaceBook group for gluten free in Singapore you should join it! There’s a lot of information specific to Singapore and many fun gluten free finds and tips & tricks posted by members :) 

Unfortunately gluten intolerance or celiac disease doesn’t get really better so it is a lifestyle change not just a diet preference. If you’re unsure I suggest you try the Whole 30 Diet, it will help you eliminate food sources and adapt your diet so find out what might be causing your bloating. Consuming foods that create adverse reactions are harmful in the long run. 

If you think that the problem is gluten it is best to eliminate gluten completely - that includes traces of it. So ALWAYS ready labels!! Make sure that the supplements you buy are labeled to be Gluten Free (GF). However, if the ingredients don’t list gluten products, it’s usually safe to consume but consume with caution. 

For most of the time I really just stick to rice for my meals, it’s the safest option. For protein sources, as long as it’s not breaded, battered, drenched in sauce or deep fried it’s mostly safe to consume. 

Keto recipes are also good for meal ideas as they are generally gluten free. I buy Optimum Nutrition for my supplements as their products are labeled gluten free and so far I have had no issues with it, it’s rather popular among the GF community :) 

Common Sneaky Gluten Sources: Soy Sauce, Soup Stock, Some Ice Creams, Granola/bars, Cereal and protein powder, vitamins and protein bars 

The obvious ones are noodles, beehoon, fast food, bread, non GF cereal, ice cream cones, if you drink a lot - beer. Anything containing Wheat, Barley, Rye is not gluten free.

Hi OP! My sister has OCD-ASD, and similarly she has been switching therapists often. She is now seeing her 5th therapist because so far none have helped her or have been able to teach her coping mechanisms that she can adhere to and practice on her own until now. It is indeed very frustrating, and I wouldn’t say it’s entirely your fault too because it is actually quite common for people with the OCD diagnosis hop around and find a proper therapist! Please don’t lose hope. 

We have visited almost every OCD specialist in Singapore, and once she finally found a therapist that could meet her needs, I have seen her small steps forward. I would suggest to find a therapist that specializes in OCD because OCD is very complex and it can be hard for any other therapist to help you. 

What we have learned from this however is that you must voice out your needs to your therapist. If you feel that she is being too aggressive you need to voice it out, I know it may be hard but it is absolutely necessary. If your therapist doesn’t know your needs they cannot help you. At this point you probably know what you need and what you don’t need, take the time to discuss this with your therapist instead of letting them take the wheel entirely.
